changes_vs_current: Rebuilt from people sources aimed at US adults instead of three expert rankings. Scope: all-time, men and women, any nationality. Averaged sources: YouGov US fame (23 players measured), 12-month Wikipedia pageviews (~95-player pool), SSRS favorite men's pro (8) and Instagram followers (5), with missing items scored as list length + 5. Computed order: Messi and Cristiano tied at 1.75 (Messi first: he leads SSRS and YouGov), Mbappé 5.5, Beckham 7.0, Haaland 7.25, Kane 8.75, Yamal 9.75, Bellingham 10.25, Salah 10.5, Pelé 10.5, Pulisic 11.5, Neymar 13.0, Zlatan 13.25, Lewandowski 14.0, Maradona 15.5, R9 16.0, Zidane 16.25, Ronaldinho 16.5, Henry 17.0. Gut-check moves: Beckham up to #3 (YouGov US fame 82%, the highest of any soccer player and #18 of all US sports personalities). Pelé up from 10th to #4 (YouGov 70%, tied with Cristiano; also first in the UK public GOAT poll). Neymar up from 12th to #6 (Instagram #3 among footballers at 241M, 5.4M pageviews; his YouGov page could not be found, so the method's missing-item penalty understates him). Mia Hamm up to #7, Rapinoe to #9 and Alex Morgan to #11 (YouGov US fame 60%, 58% and 48%; global English pageviews and the men-only SSRS and Instagram lists are what sink them). Maradona up from 15th to #8 (3.9M pageviews, 5% in the UK public poll; no YouGov page found). Wambach (#14) and Donovan (#15) stay below #12 because sources put them there: Wambach's 44% YouGov fame ties Kane and trails Haaland, and Donovan has 0.98M pageviews and no YouGov page. Vs the current list: kept Messi, Cristiano, Pelé, Maradona, Zidane and R9, but moved Cristiano from 4th to 2nd, Pelé from 3rd to 4th, Maradona from 2nd to 8th, Zidane from 6th to 22nd and R9 from 8th to 21st. Dropped 18 expert-favored legends a typical American would not name and that no people source lifts: Cruyff (1.19M views), Beckenbauer, Di Stéfano, Platini, Gerd Müller, Puskás, George Best, Garrincha, Maldini, Zico, Romário, Bobby Charlton, van Basten, Meazza, Eusébio, Iniesta, Baggio and Kopa. Added Beckham, Neymar, Mbappé, Mia Hamm, Rapinoe, Alex Morgan, Wambach, Donovan, Pulisic, Haaland, Kane, Yamal, Bellingham, Salah, Zlatan, Lewandowski, Ronaldinho and Henry. Alias fix: 'ronaldo' now belongs only to Cristiano; R9 has 'r9|brazilian ronaldo|ronaldo nazario'. 'pele' is not repeated as an alias because it matches the label key. No critic lists were used: no ties needed breaking.
confidence: High for #1-4: Messi, Cristiano, Beckham and Pelé are the four highest YouGov US fame scores (70-82%) and lead or nearly lead every other people source. Medium for #5-11. Mbappé and Haaland are strong on pageviews and SSRS, but their YouGov fame (46-48%) sits close to the roughly 40-45% floor of the contemporary-players list. Neymar's and Maradona's placements rest on pageviews and Instagram or the UK poll, because no YouGov US page could be found for either. The US women are placed by YouGov fame against weak global pageviews, so their exact slots are judgement calls. Medium-low for #12-24. Kane, Yamal, Bellingham, Salah and Lewandowski are lifted by global English pageviews and the SSRS fan poll, and YouGov shows only about 41-45% of US adults have heard of them, so a casual American may not type them. Pulisic (#18) could deserve a higher spot for a US audience. Near-misses: Hope Solo (YouGov 55% fame, but only 0.32M pageviews), Luka Modrić, Vinícius Júnior, Wayne Rooney, Carli Lloyd, Tim Howard, Clint Dempsey and Johan Cruyff. I could not get Google Trends US data or a US all-time poll covering retired players and women, so the method relies heavily on YouGov fame for the US-specific signal.
